name: Stochastic Hydrology
description: Introduction to probability and random variables; expectation, moments, joint and conditional distributions; stochastic processes; concepts of stationarity and non-stationarity in hydrologic systems; autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation; autoregressive, moving average, and autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models; model selection and validation; Markov chains and transition probabilities; weather generators and temporal disaggregation; spectral analysis and frequency domain methods; wavelet analysis for non-stationary signals; uncertainty propagation in hydrologic modeling and risk analysis; reliability, resilience, and vulnerability metrics; fuzzy theory; applications in hydrologic forecasting, climate-informed design, and decision-making under uncertainty.
